claim: Self-generated related problems (K=3-5) lift GPT-3.5-turbo by only about 1 to 4 points over 0-shot CoT in the founding paper: GSM8K 75.8 to 77.8, MATH 33.9 to 37.3, PaLM2 MATH 29.8 to 34.8. No seeds or intervals. Gap search: Luo et al. 2025 (5 models) also find a gain only on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4-turbo (+3.1, +3.5 average over ZS-CoT) and a loss on Qwen1.5-14B/72B and Llama3-70B (-1.4, -2.8, -2.5).
agent_test: Run prompt vs plain CoT at equal total tokens (count the recall tokens as output cost), 3 seeds, 500+ items, report CI.

claim: The founding gains are not reproduced by an independent group on the same model: Qin et al. find relevant self-generated examples score 71.5 GSM8K and 33.3 MATH, below a prompt that asks for unrelated (N/A) problems (75.5, 36.1) and below Yasunaga's own 0-shot (75.0). On 5 BBH tasks relevant wins by 1.3 points. Gap search: Qin replicates on Llama-2-70B, Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-14B (relevant below N/A on every model, by 2.5 to 6.3 points on GSM8K) and on CSQA, MBPP, GPQA; Luo et al. independently find Ana-Pro below ZS-CoT on three open models.
agent_test: Head-to-head on our agent: relevant recall vs N/A recall vs nothing, same token budget; the split tells whether the gain comes from relevance or from extra generation.

claim: Accuracy of the self-written examples matters for math: hand-graded MATH examples were 62% correct for relevant, 72% for N/A, 86% for random-same. Replacing demo answers with GPT-4 answers raised every arm (GSM8K relevant 71.2 to 75.2). Gap search: with GPT-4 answers the MATH relevant arm rose 37.0 to 44.4; Llama-2-70B GSM8K relevant 56.2 to 60.8.
agent_test: Add a cheap check pass on the recalled problems (re-solve each, drop disagreements) and measure the lift against unchecked recall.

claim: Method works only when the model is strong enough to write valid problems: on GSM8K ours beats fixed and retrieved 5-shot on text-davinci-002/003 (48 vs 43/47; 61 vs 54/57) but loses on davinci-001 (9 vs 10/11).
agent_test: Not needed for frontier models; record recall-validity rate on our agent's model as a precondition check.

claim: Number of recalled problems matters little beyond K=3: K=1 76.1/34.8, K=3 77.5/37.3, K=5 77.8/37.1 (GSM8K/MATH). K=1 is worse because the model leans on one exemplar.
agent_test: Use K=3 default; test K=1 vs 3 at equal tokens.

claim: Asking for diverse recalled problems beats non-diverse (GSM8K 77.8 vs 75.9; MATH 37.3 vs 35.2). Writing background knowledge first adds on code (Codeforces Acc@1 15 vs 13 for GPT-3.5, 19 vs 17 for GPT-4) but on 50 problems and 1-2 problem differences.
agent_test: Include a diversity instruction in the recall prompt; ablate it.

claim: In the founding qualitative check, 15 of 50 correct answers had flawed or irrelevant recalled problems, and 28 of 50 wrong answers had good exemplars: failure is mostly generalization or over-reliance, not bad recall.
agent_test: Log per-run recall quality and correlate with correctness on our agent.

claim: The benefit may come from the process of writing problems inside the same prompt, not from the examples: Decoupled use of the same examples gives about zero-shot accuracy, Integrated gives +4.7 (GPT-4o GSM8K 49.9 to 54.6, MATH 33.3 to 37.9) across 5 models. Gap search: re-opened. Holds on 5 models and 1/2/4 shots (Llama-3.3-70B 4-shot Integrated 38.2 vs Decoupled 32.4); still one group, temperature 0, one run.
agent_test: Compare in-prompt recall vs recall in a separate call then fed back, at equal tokens.

claim: Related self-generation methods show small positive gains that are uneven: Self-ICL +3.1 average over 23 BBH-type tasks but Temporal Sequences falls 57.6 to 35.6; SG-ICL one self-generated sample worth about 0.6 gold samples; generated knowledge +8 to +11 on commonsense with a small model.
agent_test: Treat self-generated context as a modest, task-dependent help with a real loss tail; gate it per task type.

claim: A separate third-party comparison reports analogical prompting below plain CoT: GPT-4o-mini average 56.0 vs 60.7 (MATH 65.4 vs 78.3), with near-identical deltas on two other backbones; CodeSim tables show Analogical below CoT on code. Prompt wording and implementation are unknown. Gap search: Zhang's prompt is not in the paper (supplementary only), so the cause is not isolated; Luo et al. show the same sign on three open models but the opposite sign on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4-turbo.
agent_test: Check that any recall prompt does not displace the model's native reasoning on strong chat models; A/B against plain CoT on every task family.

claim: Correct-label demos matter little on classification (random labels cost 0 to 5 points) but correct answers matter in math with open outputs, where wrong recalled solutions hurt.
agent_test: Do not assume exemplar correctness is irrelevant for open-answer tasks; verify recalled solutions.

claim: Chain-of-thought exemplars can be wrong in steps and still keep 80-90% of valid-CoT gains (older models), and 1 to 2 wrong demos of 8 did not hurt Auto-CoT; but similarity-retrieved demos made errors repeat (46.9% vs 25.8% still unresolved).
agent_test: Prefer diverse recalled problems over many near copies of the target; avoid error contagion from one wrong near-neighbour.

claim: Relational transfer in LLMs is brittle outside the training distribution: GPT models fall as letter-string alphabets are permuted while humans stay stable; failures come from missing relation information or poor application.
agent_test: Test recall-then-solve on counterfactual variants of tasks (altered symbols/rules) to see if recalled analogies transfer.

claim: Searching distant domains rather than same-type problems can raise novelty and diversity (diversity +90 to 173%, novel solutions over 50% vs 1.6% baseline) and structured analogy retrieval raised geometry proof success under a fixed verifier (GPT-5 88 to 96).
agent_test: On a creative or open task, compare same-type recall vs cross-domain recall at equal tokens, scored by blind judge.

claim: Step-back abstraction and Thought Propagation are related prompt forms: step-back PaLM-2L Physics 66.4 to 73.2, but on GPT-4 plain CoT (82.9) is nearly as strong as step-back (84.5); TP raises shortest-path optimal rate 0.33 to 0.65 on GPT-3.5 with extra calls.
agent_test: Gains shrink as the base model is stronger; budget-match any multi-call analogy method.

claim: Token cost: analogical prompting adds output tokens (recalled problems and solutions) and removes input exemplar tokens; no paper reports cost-matched comparisons with plain CoT plus self-consistency. Gap search: Qin Table 12 has SC5 (77.6) above relevant recall (74.8) on Llama-3.1-8B but not token-matched; Wang et al. 2024 show CoT-SC wins at equal 10k-token budgets over other strategies (AP not included). Still no AP vs CoT-SC token-matched test.
agent_test: Run at equal total tokens vs CoT-SC; this is the main gap.

claim: Few-shot worked demos hurt reasoning-trained models: with R1-style optimal demos, AIME'25 accuracy drops about 6 to 16 points at one demo and up to 35 at three; GPQA-Diamond 1 to 5 and 4 to 8 points. No paper tests self-generated analogical recall on such models.
agent_test: Run recall-then-solve vs direct on a reasoning-trained backbone, 3 seeds; expect harm; keep O7 off by default there.

claim: Turning demos into explicit insights first, then solving, lifts reasoning models: AIME'25 R1-Distill-14B 50.0 to 54.0 (I2S) and 60.0 (I2S+); GPQA 59.5 to 63.0; beats majority@3 at equal question-conditioned calls, but majority@32 is slightly higher on AIME'25.
agent_test: Recall a strategy (not a worked answer), then solve; compare with CoT-SC at equal tokens.

claim: Analogical prompting tracks backbone strength: gains over zero-shot CoT appear on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4-turbo (+3.1, +3.5 average over 8 tasks) and reverse on Qwen1.5-14B/72B and Llama3-70B (-1.4, -2.8, -2.5). Three independent groups (Qin, Gwak, Luo) agree that the effect is small and model-dependent.
agent_test: Gate O7 by a quick pilot of 20 items on the actual backbone: recall vs plain.

claim: Loss tail: Analogical Prompting loses most on short-answer symbolic tasks (BBH colored objects: Qwen1.5-72B 50.8 vs ZS-CoT 78.8; Llama3-70B 69.6 vs 85.0; temporal sequences 43.6 vs 51.6), and CoT beats AP on Tracking Shuffled Objects in Gemini 1.0. Drops may be answer-format failures; cause not isolated.
agent_test: Log per-task delta of O7 vs plain; check whether failures are format errors by re-grading with a lenient extractor.

claim: Fixed or one-time correct example sets match or beat per-item recall on the same math tasks at lower cost (Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K: ICLmath 80.2, ICLbio 81.0, SC5 77.6, relevant recall 74.8; GPT-3.5 mean 56.3 and 56.4 vs 52.4 for relevant).
agent_test: Compare a verified fixed bank of worked problems against per-item recall at equal tokens.

claim: Cross-domain relational analogy search raises diversity and novelty of open research solutions (solution Vendi +90 to 173%; binary novelty 50-69% vs 22-38% cross-domain and 2-9% no-domain; humans pick AR as more novel 78%, kappa 0.445) at 2 LLM calls. No same-domain recall arm, no correctness task.
agent_test: Add a same-type recall arm and blind human judges on our own idea tasks.

claim: No paper tests analogical prompting on counterfactual or novel-rule variants, on post-cutoff benchmarks, or with same-model verification of recalled problems; as of 2026-11 these are open. Related evidence: counterfactual letter-string studies show GPT-3 to 4 drop sharply while humans do not.
agent_test: Run O7 on counterfactual variants of our tasks and on a post-cutoff set; add a re-solve check on recalled problems and log cost.
